nary_nodes.label: Julian Nagelsmann resigns as Germany coach
evidence: Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann has been asked to step down after the team’s early World Cup exit, the country’s football association DFB announced on Friday, saying the 38-year-old had agreed to go following talks with senior officials.

nary_nodes.label: DFB announces Nagelsmann's resignation
evidence: Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann has been asked to step down after the team’s early World Cup exit, the country’s football association DFB announced on Friday, saying the 38-year-old had agreed to go following talks with senior officials.

nary_nodes.label: Germany's early exit from World Cup 2026
evidence: Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann has been asked to step down after the team’s early World Cup exit

nary_nodes.label: DFB thanks Julian Nagelsmann for his work
evidence: “The German Football Association expressly thanks Julian Nagelsmann for his work since September 2023,” DFB President Bernd Neuendorf said in a statement.

nary_nodes.label: Bernd Neuendorf praises Nagelsmann's qualities
evidence: “He is characterised by a high-level of commitment and extraordinary ambition. Julian Nagelsmann is also an extremely responsible and sincere person whom we all value.”

nary_nodes.label: Bild reports Nagelsmann offered severance package
evidence: German tabloid Bild reported that Nagelsmann took part in a three-hour meeting at DFB headquarters in Frankfurt on Thursday in which he was reportedly offered a seven-million-euro ($8m) severance package, approximately one year’s salary, to leave the position.

nary_nodes.label: Nagelsmann forced to step down as coach
evidence: Nagelsmann becomes just the second national coach in German history to be forced to step down after predecessor Hansi Flick suffered the same fate in 2023.

nary_nodes.label: Hansi Flick forced to step down as coach
evidence: predecessor Hansi Flick suffered the same fate in 2023.

nary_nodes.label: Nagelsmann's statement on his difficult decision
evidence: “The decision was anything but easy for me,” Nagelsmann said in a statement.

nary_nodes.label: Nagelsmann states team success was his priority
evidence: “My top priority has always been the success of the team. After such a bitter disappointment, it deserves the chance of a new beginning.”

nary_nodes.label: Nagelsmann apologizes to fans
evidence: “I am sorry and hurt from the bottom of my heart that we disappointed you and couldn’t give you any more football nights at this World Cup,” Nagelsmann added, apologising to fans.

nary_nodes.label: Germany's third successive World Cup flop
evidence: Germany’s defeat by Paraguay in Boston marked a third successive World Cup flop.

nary_nodes.label: Germany's group stage exit at Russia 2018
evidence: The four-time World Cup winners suffered exits at the group stage at Russia 2018

nary_nodes.label: Germany's group stage exit in Qatar
evidence: and in Qatar four years ago.

nary_nodes.label: Germany's last knockout win in 2014
evidence: They have not won a knockout match or kept a clean sheet at the tournament since the 2014 final, a 1-0 win over Argentina in Brazil.

nary_nodes.label: Jurgen Klopp considered for Germany coach
evidence: Nagelsmann’s departure leaves the door open for former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp, the federation’s preferred candidate, to take over.

nary_nodes.label: DFB to begin discussions with Jurgen Klopp
evidence: The DFB said discussions would begin with Klopp, the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund manager, who has said he is “fundamentally willing” to take over as Germany coach.

nary_nodes.label: Jurgen Klopp willing to take Germany coach job
evidence: who has said he is “fundamentally willing” to take over as Germany coach.

evidence: Klopp, who left Liverpool in 2024 after a hugely successful stay during which he won the Champions League and Premier League

evidence: The 59-year-old remains hugely popular in Germany and has been engaged as a pundit on German TV throughout coverage of the World Cup.
